items.speaker: other
items.question: Most of our vans are fairly new, but we've still got eleven 2009 Chevy Express vans out on the road. Will your plug-in tracker work on those, or is that a wiring job?

oracle.expected_behavior_note: Two current documents disagree and nothing settles it. The installation guide (revision C, 8 June 2026) says the plug-in OBD-II connection is supported on light vehicles from model year 2008 onward. The vehicle compatibility list (edition 2026-06) gives gasoline vans, Chevrolet Express among them, a minimum model year of 2010, and sends older light vehicles to the three-wire kit. A 2009 van falls between the two. The seller must not say flatly that the plug-in harness works and must not say flatly that it does not: the honest line is that one document says from 2008 and the other from 2010, so it needs confirming with Field Engineering. What is certain is the floor: the vans can be tracked either way, because the three-wire kit works on any vehicle, though with it there is no odometer, fuel level or fault codes from the vehicle.

required_facts.text: The installation guide says the plug-in connection is supported from model year 2008.
The vehicle compatibility list gives gasoline vans a minimum model year of 2010.

optional_facts.text: With the three-wire kit the unit reports position, trips and ignition time but no odometer, fuel level or fault codes.
Light vehicles older than the minimum model year are fitted with the KH-3W kit.

forbidden_claims.text: States flatly that the plug-in harness works on the 2009 vans.
States flatly that the plug-in harness does not work on the 2009 vans.
Invents a rule for which of the two documents wins.
Says the 2009 vans cannot be tracked at all.

oracle.expected_role: seller (account executive) speaking to the prospect, first person

known_conflicts.topic: Earliest model year for the plug-in OBD-II connection on light vehicles

acceptable_inference: Offering to confirm with Field Engineering before the order is placed.
Saying the newer vans take the plug-in harness without any doubt.

items.question: same customer also runs six kalmar ottawa yard tractors, 2019 models. which harness part do i put on the order for those, and is there any vehicle data that won't come through on them?

oracle.expected_behavior_note: The vehicle compatibility list gives a harness for each vehicle group. Yard tractors (Kalmar Ottawa T2 among the examples) have the black 9-pin connector and take harness KH-9B, from model year 2010. The odometer is not sent on them, so engine hours are used for service schedules; fuel level, engine hours and fault codes do come through. The trap is the model year: the green-connector KH-9G is for road trucks from 2016, and a 2019 yard tractor still takes KH-9B. The other harnesses in the list (KH-16Y, KH-16J, KH-3W) belong to other groups. The installation guide's table says the same (black 9-pin: heavy trucks before 2016, yard tractors).

required_facts.text: Yard tractors take harness KH-9B (black 9-pin).
The odometer is not sent on yard tractors; engine hours are used instead.

optional_facts.text: The installation guide also lists yard tractors under the black 9-pin harness.

forbidden_claims.text: Gives the green-connector harness for road trucks from 2016, because the tractors are 2019 models.
Gives the three-wire kit, as if a yard tractor had no diagnostic connector.
Gives a harness that belongs to another vehicle group.
Says fuel level, engine hours or fault codes are missing on yard tractors.

oracle.expected_role: assistant advising the seller privately; an explanation for the seller, not a line addressed to the prospect
acceptable_inference: Advising that service schedules for these tractors be set on engine hours.
